read: turns 00:04 (Amal: شو اليوم؟) to 1:02:40 (Amal: باي.) - all 972 lines, in order
coverage_note: Whole file read. Holes/garbles: 06:38-07:20 date and clock are Latin-transliterated (tisa asha, Sa alaat ila tult, Intayn); 12:13 Amal's colour fix is garbled (بدائية); 24:05-24:38 the root قصد is transcribed as أزد/أزت/مهم; 24:50-25:16 بتداي/بيتايوكي = بيدايقوكي with ق dropped; 26:49-27:05 بعين/بعيم = بقيم (S4); 30:21 كيك؟ and 39:59 أكره كاسته are unreadable; 38:33 Amal 'أشياءي نوع الإل' unreadable (no row); 42:00-42:15 hand/إيد exchange garbled (Dan's, eat, ear); 42:15-42:29 Medi talks to a passer-by in English; 51:36 Amal 'سائل' and 55:30-55:33 'بفيت'/'أنا واعي' unreadable; 55:05 'أبن كتير' and 56:04 'بفزت' garbled. Not filed as errors: S4 sound slips (03:11 جهزت/جهّزت shadda, 15:02 أزعشتك, 29:46 سكرتي self-fixed, 32:58/33:11 بتزلي for بتضلي, 33:41 سهوني for صحوني, 43:10 'letters order' on انكسرت, 44:18 اثنعش, 52:52 اشي/إشي vowel); 05:58 الأربعاء→الخميس self-fixed before Amal's لا; 16:39 and 25:38 'كم مرة؟' were listening misunderstandings (هديك المرة / الفعل الجاي), not filed; 22:24 'تكوني or مبسوطة?' and 43:32 'كان عمرها أو عمرها كان؟' and 36:58 past of بنكسر were grammar questions he asked before erring, not filed; 51:20 'bones' he never attempted and Amal did not supply, not filed. 'air conditioning' (12:53, 53:14, 53:29) is not on her sheet and Amal herself said الـ air conditioning تبعي, so no tier-3 row. Long stretches 03:40-05:52, 17:06-18:06, 46:08-48:13, 57:27-1:02:33 are English discussion.

rows.medi_said: كيف كان الـ-- كيف كان العروسة؟ عروس؟
rows.why: He asked how the wedding was using عروسة/عروس (bride); Amal supplied عرس (wedding); he repeated عروس again at 01:57.

He said زعمت (I claimed) for عزمت (I invited); Amal corrected after prompting him to try a few times. Root letters swapped, so it may be an S4 slip, but زعم is a real different word and he flagged it himself at 04:05.
He shaped the verb as صلاح- (long a) instead of صلّح-; Amal recast صلحته. Could be F2/F3 sound shape rather than vocab; same pattern again at 10:34 (صلاحني).

rows.medi_said: Is it raki? What was electricity?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for the word for electricity and Amal supplied كهربا (sheet: electricity | Kahraba | كهربا).

rows.medi_said: كراجي. This is a new word. It's not gonna be on the list.
rows.why: He repeated her new word كهربجي as كراجي (a non-word / 'garage guy') twice (09:30, 09:39); Amal re-said كهربجي. New word she had just taught, so a low-stakes miss.

rows.amal_said: You said صلح which is fix. You did wha-- did you wanna say he helped me?
rows.why: He used صلّح (fix) to mean 'he helped me'; Amal asked whether he meant helped and he then produced ساعدني (sheet: help | Saa3ed | ساعد).
rows.english: The electrician helped me a little

rows.why: He said دولت for 'I stayed'; Amal said 'what?' and supplied ضليت (sheet: i stayed/kept | Ana dallait | ضليت). Wrong vowel shape of a verb he knows, beyond a ض/د slip; he repeated دولت at 12:41.
Literal 'one more' as واحد أكتر; Amal gave كمان واحد (sheet: also / more / too | Kamaan | كمان; one more time | Kaman marra).

rows.medi_said: So I add his بزيء، بزياد،
rows.why: He fumbled the form of 'I add' as بزياد; Amal supplied بزيد.
Groping for 'I remove' (شول ~ بشيل?); Amal supplied بقيم (sheet: i remove / take away | Ana ba2eem | بقيم). He then said بعين/بعيم (ق dropped, S4).
He said بخسر (I lose) for بكسر (I break); Amal: 'close - بكسر'. خ for ك could be an S4 slip but بخسر is a real different word and he repeated it at 28:06/28:18/28:26.

rows.medi_said: Is it يسكر and يسكري؟ يسكرو؟ اكسر. Yeah اكسر.
rows.amal_said: The K is before the S.
rows.why: Command of كسر said with swapped root letters (يسكر ~ سكّر 'close'); Amal pointed out the letter order. He also started with a y- prefix for the command (B10) but self-fixed to اكسر.

rows.medi_said: Is it, is it Dan's hand, right?
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked for 'hand' (transcript garbled: Dan's/eat = إيدها/إيد) and Amal confirmed; he then used إيدها at 42:53 (sheet: hand / arm | Eed (F) | إيد).
He said eleven (إحداعش) for twelve; Amal said '12. إتناش' (sheet: twelve | tna3sh | تنعش). His retry at 44:18 اثنعش is MSA-ish sound shape, let pass.
He made 'present tense' feminine (مضارعة, again المضارعة at 44:41); Amal said مضارع. Wrong gender form of a noun he knows.

rows.amal_said: انكسر. Did it actually like break?
rows.why: He used انكسر for the AC 'broke from the heat'; Amal: 'my issue is with the verb itself... كسر is physical', stop working is خرب/خربان (sheet: not working properly | 5arbaan | خربان; i break down | Ana ba5rab | بخرب). She had pre-warned at 48:49.
rows.english: It broke (stopped working) from the heat

rows.why: He said تعبي (heard as تعبني 'tired me') for تبعي ('mine', which Amal had just given him at 48:29); Amal asked 'do you wanna say the air conditioning tired me?'. Letter swap producing a different word.
rows.english: because my air conditioning was broken

rows.medi_said: إن و-- إن. الف-الفعلات. الفعلات إن.
rows.why: Invented plural فعلات for فعل; Amal supplied أفعال (sheet: verb – verbs | Fe3el | فعل; broken plural pattern, A9 territory but an invented plural = tier 2 per brief).
Asked كيف الجو عندكم اليوم at 2:40 pm, he answered الليلة (tonight; sheet: tonight | ellaile | الليلة) and dropped the adjective (sheet: hot (weather) | Shoab | شوب); Amal just said عن جد؟.
rows.english: Today the weather is very hot

rows.why: قربان (sacrifice) for خربان (not working; sheet: not working properly | 5arbaan | خربان); Amal let it pass. Could be an S4 ق/خ slip - he said خربان correctly at 48:58.

rows.medi_said: tisa asha. Oh no, that's right. Yeah, asha tisa.
rows.why: Date said month-first (nine ten); Amal: 'first we say عشرة تسعة' (day then month).

rows.amal_said: I just repeated what you said. ألفين ستة وعشرين.
rows.why: He could not finish the year and dropped an English placeholder; Amal supplied ألفين ستة وعشرين.

rows.medi_said: Sa alaat ila nun-- ila tult.
rows.why: Clock time 2:40 said with تلاتة; Amal asked تلات أو تنتين؟, he fixed to Intayn and she recast تنتين إلا تلت (07:22).

rows.medi_said: مهندس-- Do you guys say مهندس كهرباء؟
rows.why: Idafa 'the electricity engineer': he left el- off the second noun; Amal recast مهندس الكهربا (el- on the owner word only). He was also half-asking.

rows.amal_said: صلحني would be he fixed me. Like you, you were who's being fixed.
rows.why: For 'fixed (it) for me' he put the object ending on the verb (صلاحني = fixed me); Amal had offered صلح لي at 10:30 and explained. Moot once he switched to ساعدني, so low.

Masculine colour adjective after feminine بلوزة; Amal's fix is garbled in the transcript (بدائية) but he then said 'وردنية that's right'. Sheet has pink (m/f) | Zahri | زهري, so the word itself may also be off.

rows.medi_said: بس واحد-- وحدة كلمة صح و
rows.why: 'One word': the number/adjective must follow the noun; Amal recast بس كلمة وحدة and he repeated it.
'I annoyed you' said with an extra -ti- (زعجتيك, the you-f ending) instead of I-past زعجتك; Amal recast زعجتك or أزعجتك. His أزعشتك at 15:02 is S4.
'You got annoyed with me': he stopped at انزعجتي without the fixed preposition; Amal prompted (ليش ما؟) and he produced مني, then انزعجتي مني (16:22) = Perfect. انزعج takes من (Amal 14:35).
Talking to إنتي he used masculine participle مزعوج; Amal asked إنتي أو انت؟ and he fixed to مزعوجة (18:54).

rows.medi_said: And then باز is not بازوج, بازيجيني هدول اليوم.
rows.why: 'Many things annoy me': plural subject needs بزعجوني; he said a singular بيزعجني shape. Amal recast twice; he acknowledged 'it's plural'.
rows.english: Many things annoy me these days

rows.why: Second attempt at the same sentence still singular (بيزعجيني); Amal recast بزعجوني again and he then said بيزعجوني.
'These days' with singular اليوم after هدول; Amal supplied the plural أيام; he admitted he had written أيام.
'Are you sure THAT you didn't annoy him': he used اللي (the one that) for the complement 'that'; Amal asked Why اللي؟ then said إنو مش اللي.
rows.english: Are you sure that you guys didn't annoy him?

rows.amal_said: بس مبسوطة إذا ما بشوف هيك.
rows.why: After إذا ما he dropped the b- (أشوفك); Amal recast إذا ما بشوفك مبسوطة and he repeated it (22:31). Note: bucket B3 says drop after iza, but her fix here keeps the b- in this negative conditional; filing under B3 as the iza/b- rule.
rows.english: if I don't see you happy

rows.why: 'Don't be annoyed with them' given as a positive command إنزعجي; Amal prompted 'so don't be' and he fixed to ما تنزعج / ما تنزعجي (23:24-23:32).
'They didn't mean to upset you' (مش قصدهم ...): he kept the b- on the following verb (بيدايقوكي); Amal recast يدايقوكي without b-. The ق is dropped throughout (S4, not filed).
rows.english: They didn't mean to upset you

rows.why: 'They broke' with the she-ending كسرت; Amal echoed it questioningly and he fixed to هم كسروا (28:47), which she confirmed.
In 'you keep breaking my plates' his verb came out without the بت- prefix (زري); Amal: 'I didn't hear the t' and he said بتكسري (33:31). Transcript of his line is garbled.
'His cups' given as singular كاسته; Amal recast the plural كاساته (transcript كساته). Sheet: cup | Kaasa | كاسة.
'His cup': he said كاسته, Amal said كاسه; he repeated كاسته at 40:35. Her possessive form of كاسة here is كاسه, though she treats it as feminine for the verb.
'His cup broke': feminine subject كاسة needs انكسرت; he said انكسر, Amal recast, he asked why and she confirmed 'because it's female' (41:00).
'When she was 12' = كان عمرها; he switched كان to كانت to match هي, but the verb agrees with عمر (m). Amal: لأ، كان عمرها صح.

rows.medi_said: Uh, هي بينكسو-- بينكسر. هو بينكسر.
rows.why: He gave the he-form بينكسر for هي; Amal said هو (that's the he form) and he fixed to هي بتنكسر (45:46).

rows.medi_said: ما بكسر-- أنا ما ... بكسور-- بكسر، أنا ما بكسر، اشي
rows.why: 'I have never broken anything' said in the present (ما بكسر) because he thought أبداً forces present; Amal asked بكسر أو كسرت؟, said 'who said that?', and he produced أنا أبدًا ما كسرت ولا اشي (52:44).
'I didn't sleep well': he negated the adverb with مش instead of the verb with ما; Amal offered ما نمت منيح and he repeated it.
'I am annoyed' given with the active participle مزعج (annoying); Amal recast أنا مزعوج (he said 'No. مزعوج' at the same moment) and then checked he knew مزعج = I'm annoying.

rows.medi_said: is it بزور بنكسر؟ بنكسر. أكسر. Okay.
rows.why: Listing the last verb pair he said أكسر without the b-; Amal recast بكسر and بنكسر.
'A video on YouTube' with لـ instead of على; Amal did not react. Best reading only.
rows.english: I watched a video on YouTube

rows.medi_said: ما، ما يكون، uh, كهربج-- uh, كهربجي، هو مهندس
rows.why: 'He is not an electrician, he's an engineer': negating a noun needs مش, he used ما يكون; Amal let it pass (she was listening to his English explanation).
rows.english: He's not an electrician, he's an engineer

rows.why: 'Today I'm wearing' as the b-present بلبس rather than the state participle لابس; Amal accepted it (sheet has i wear / i'm putting on | Balbes | بلبس, so low).

rows.medi_said: بس كلمة-- بس فعل، اه، تنين،
rows.why: 'Two verbs' with noun + تنين instead of the dual فعلين; Amal's reply (بس فعلاً) is not a clear fix.

rows.medi_said: أيام. I even wrote أيام. هدول أيام.
rows.why: After the plural fix he said هدول أيام without el- on the noun after the demonstrative; Amal moved on.
'You guys didn't annoy HIM': the object ending -ه is missing on أزعجتو; Amal only addressed the اللي/إنو error in that sentence.
'With them' after ما تنزعجي said as preposition + free pronoun (من هم) instead of منهم; Amal moved to the next sentence. May be a transcription spacing artefact.

rows.medi_said: الـ أول الـ فعل، الـ أول الكلمة.
rows.why: 'The beginning of the verb' as an idafa: the first word must not take el- (الأول الفعل); Amal only said Mm.
rows.english: the beginning of the verb / the first letter of the word

rows.why: Plain present 'they break' without the b- (يكسروا) in the conjugation run; Amal said Nice and moved on.
You-plural past given with the MSA ending -تم instead of Levantine -توا (cf. his own كسرتوا at 29:18); Amal let it pass.
For هي/هو he produced بينكسري (a you-f ending on a he-prefix); Amal redirected to إنتو rather than fixing it (she fixed the هي form later at 45:38).
'We get broken' should carry both the n- of we and the n- of the in-verb (بننكسر); he said بنكسر and Amal went on to say the we-forms are rarely used.
Replying to يلا بشوفك he said ما شوفتك (I didn't see you) for 'see you'; Amal just said bye. Likely a mis-hearing of منشوفك by the transcript, so low.
